sections.heading: Gradient of a Straight Line
sections.html:
• Measure of the steepness of a straight line

  • Gradient=y2−y1x2−x1Gradient = \frac{y_2 - y_1 }{x_2 - x_1 }Gradient=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​

sections.heading: Equation of a Line
sections.html:
Ax+By=C(General Equation of Line) Ax + By = C \quad \text{(General Equation of Line)} Ax+By=C(General Equation of Line)xa+yb=1(Intercept Form) \frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1 \quad \text{(Intercept Form)} ax​+by​=1(Intercept Form)y=mx+c(Slope–Intercept Form) y = mx + c \quad \text{(Slope–Intercept Form)} y=mx+c(Slope–Intercept Form)

  • m = gradient

  • c = y-intercept (the point the graph meets the y-axis)

sections.heading: Midpoint of Graph
sections.html: Midpoint=(x1+x22, y1+y22) Midpoint = \left( \frac{x_1 + x_2 }{2},\ \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2} \right) Midpoint=(2x1​+x2​​, 2y1​+y2​​)

sections.heading: Length between Two Points
sections.html: Distance=(x2−x1)2+(y2−y1)2 Distance = \sqrt{\left( x_2 - x_1 \right)^{2} + \left( y_2 - y_1 \right)^{2}} Distance=(x2​−x1​)2+(y2​−y1​)2​

sections.heading: Cartesian Coordinate System
sections.html:
• They are written in the (x,y) for

  • Quadrant 1: (x,y)

  • Quadrant 2: (-x,y)

  • Quadrant 3: (-x,-y)

  • Quadrant 4: (x,-y)

sections.heading: Sketching Graphs
sections.html:
• Step 1: Plot the y-intercept (c) on the graph

  • Step 2: Substitute x values (whole number values) into the equation and solve for y

  • Step 3: The substituted x value is the x coordinate, and the solved y value is the y coordinate

  • Step 4: Repeat for 4 more values and draw a straight line connecting these points

How to Derive Equation of Line from Graph

Find the gradient of (0,7)(0,7)(0,7) and (4,4)(4,4)(4,4):

m=y2−y1x2−x1m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}m=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​

m=4−74−0m = \frac{4 - 7}{4 - 0}m=4−04−7​

m=−34m = \frac{-3}{4}m=4−3​

Equation of the line: y=mx+cy = mx + cy=mx+c

y=−34x+cy = -\tfrac{3}{4}x + cy=−43​x+c

Substitute (0,7)(0,7)(0,7):

7=−34(0)+c7 = -\tfrac{3}{4}(0) + c7=−43​(0)+c

7=c7 = c7=c

Therefore, y=−34x+7y = -\tfrac{3}{4}x + 7y=−43​x+7

sections.heading: Parallel Lines
sections.html:
• Two lines are parallel if they share the same gradient but different y-intercepts

  • For eg, y=3x+5 and y=3x+12y = 3x + 5 \ \text{and} \ y = 3x + 12y=3x+5 and y=3x+12

  • Since the gradient of both lines is the same, and they have different y-intercepts, they are parallel to each other

sections.heading: Perpendicular Lines
sections.html:
• Two Lines are perpendicular if they meet at 90º

  • If Line A has a gradient m, then the gradient of Line B is -1/m

  • For eg, y=2x+4 and y=−12x+5y = 2x+4 \ \text{and} \ y = \frac{-1}{2}x + 5y=2x+4 and y=2−1​x+5

  • Two lines are perpendicular if the gradient of one line is the negative reciprocal of the other

sections.heading: Perpendicular Bisectors
sections.html:
• Perpendicular Bisector is a line that intersects another line at its midpoint, and lies at an angle of 90º

  • Example:

    Point A has coordinates (7,−17)(7, -17)(7,−17)

    Point B has coordinates (19,−11)(19, -11)(19,−11)

    We want the equation of the perpendicular bisector of ABABAB.

    Step 1: Midpoint

    M=(x1+x22,y1+y22)M = \left( \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2} \right)M=(2x1​+x2​​,2y1​+y2​​)

    M=(7+192,−17+(−11)2)M = \left( \frac{7 + 19}{2}, \frac{-17 + (-11)}{2} \right)M=(27+19​,2−17+(−11)​)

    M=(262,−282)M = \left( \frac{26}{2}, \frac{-28}{2} \right)M=(226​,2−28​)

    M=(13,−14)M = (13, -14)M=(13,−14)

    Step 2: Gradient of ABABAB

    mAB=y2−y1x2−x1m_{AB} = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}mAB​=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​

    mAB=−11−(−17)19−7m_{AB} = \frac{-11 - (-17)}{19 - 7}mAB​=19−7−11−(−17)​

    mAB=612=12m_{AB} = \frac{6}{12} = \tfrac{1}{2}mAB​=126​=21​

    Step 3: Gradient of perpendicular bisector

    m⊥=−1mAB=−2m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{m_{AB}} = -2m⊥​=−mAB​1​=−2

    Step 4: Equation of perpendicular bisector

    y−(−14)=−2(x−13)y - (-14) = -2(x - 13)y−(−14)=−2(x−13)

    y+14=−2x+26y + 14 = -2x + 26y+14=−2x+26

    y=−2x+12y = -2x + 12y=−2x+12

    Therefore, the equation of the perpendicular bisector is:

    y=−2x+12\boxed{y = -2x + 12}y=−2x+12​
